scenes.say: When you run a performance test, what tells you if your system actually passes? Let's break down the single most important idea.

scenes.label: Throughput
scenes.sub: Requests handled per second. Reveals capacity.
scenes.say: Throughput is the number of requests your system handles each second. It's the best indicator of capacity under load.

scenes.label: Latency
scenes.sub: How fast responses return. Use p95 or p99.
scenes.say: Latency measures how fast your system responds. Focus on the ninety-fifth or ninety-ninth percentile—those slowest requests matter for real users.
Combine throughput, latency, and error rate. These three define your performance testing goals and show if your system meets expectations.
Load tests check how your system performs under normal traffic. Stress tests push it past its limits to find where it breaks.

scenes.question: Why not just average latency?
scenes.right: Averages hide outliers. Percentiles show real user impact.
scenes.say: Don't rely only on average latency. It hides outliers. Use percentiles to see how real users experience your system.
